subject: Post-call recap: Quantacorp inference requirements & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ellis Johnson <ellis@quantacorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Aug 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Quantacorp inference requirements & next steps

Hi Ellis — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap so we all have the same picture and a proposed set of next steps.

Summary of pain / goals you described
- Customer-facing summarization pipeline for support tickets (sensitive PII) and real-time chat assistance.
- Current latency and cost are preventing full replacement of legacy infra; you want parity (or better) at comparable TCO.
- Need predictable SLAs for response time during peak business hours (EMEA + US).

Quantitative targets you confirmed on the call
- Target p95 generation latency: ~120 ms for 512-token prompts (soft).
- Steady-state throughput target: 250 RPS across API surface; burst to 750–900 RPS for short windows.
- Availability target: 99.9% (SLA discussion will formalize).

Model & data constraints
- Preferred model family: Llama-70B fine-tuned in-house (they may consider a 34B variant).
- Must support customer-managed keys and run in a VPC/private deployment.
- Retention & audit: logs retained 30 days; need SOC2 evidence.

Proposed deployment topology (initial recommendation)
- Redwood Dedicated cluster in us-west-2 (private) with reserved capacity; start with 40x H100 80GB-equivalent capacity for primary surface.
- Multi-variant routing: 70B full precision as primary; 34B or int8 quantized 70B as fallback when queue depth increases.
- KV/prefix cache at the serving layer for session-based chats (warm cache for top 20% prefixes).
- Autoscale policy: maintain latency SLO with aggressive scale-up for bursts, scheduled scale-up during known peak windows.
- Network: cross-AZ placement with regional routing and failover to a second region for DR.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Please confirm the p95 and RPS numbers above (reply-all).
2) Ellis: can you share the procurement contact for contract and terms? (you mentioned procurement@quantacorp.com)
3) Karthik / Laura: can the infra/arch team sketch a 1-page topology diagram + rough cost/throughput estimate by EOD Aug 9?
4) Schedule a 60-minute architecture deep-dive (suggest Aug 11 or 12) — I'll send a calendar invite after we confirm availability.

Attachments: high-level sketch and our default mutual action plan (attached).

Thanks — Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ellis Johnson <ellis@quantacorp.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Quantacorp inference requirements & next steps — topology & perf notes

Marissa / Ellis / Laura — quick technical readout and recommended starting point. High-level assumptions: 70B Llama variant, typical prompt+response length ~= 512 tokens, tokenization overhead ~5%. We modeled with Redwood runtime profiling using AWQ and int8 pipelines where applicable.

Option A — H100-focused (performance-first)
- Cluster: 40x H100 80GB-equivalent (or 32x H100 w/ additional NVMe cache)
- Serving config: per-GPU steady-state throughput ~8–10 RPS (70B FP16 w/ KV cache warm). With 40 GPUs gives ~320–400 RPS steady; headroom for bursts with autoscale.
- p95 latency: ~90–140 ms depending on batching window; we can tune down to ~120 ms p95 by keeping batching windows small and enabling continuous batching with latency SLO enforcement.
- Memory: KV cache budget ~120–200 GB (depends on session stickiness); recommend Redis-like external cache + local hot cache in serving nodes.

Option B — Mixed cluster (cost-conscious)
- Cluster: 24x H100 + 40x L40s (or an array of L4/H800 alternatives) with model-slicing + multi-variant routing.
- Serving config: primary 70B quantized (AWQ/4-bit) on H100 for hard SLOs; 34B or 70B-int8 on L40s for mid/low latency requests. Per-node throughput varies: H100 int8 ~12–14 RPS (higher with fused kernels), L40s ~4–6 RPS for quantized 34B.
- p95 latency: ~130–200 ms depending on traffic mix; good tradeoff for ~30–50% cost savings over Option A.

Other technical notes
- Quantization: AWQ/NGGP/LLM.int4 offers strong density but needs per-prompt quality validation. Recommend A/B quality eval sets (we'll run the customer's test prompts through both FP16 and 4-bit variants).
- Batching strategy: dynamic batching at 8–32 tokens/window with per-route latency caps. Continuous KV cache + prefix caching for conversational sessions improves effective throughput ~1.8–2x for repeat prefixes.
- Kernel selection: Redwood runtime will pick fused attention kernels and sequence-length-aware tiling; we expect throughput gains vs generic runtimes.

Recommended next steps (concrete)
1) Approve load test: 72-hour soak with synthetic distribution (70% steady 250 RPS, 20% 400 RPS, 10% 800 RPS bursts). Redwood will provide the harness.
2) Quality validation: provide a 500-prompt eval set to quantify delta between FP16 and quantized variants.
3) Cost sketch: we'll deliver a 3-line cost estimate for Option A/B + incremental per-burst pricing by EOD Aug 10.

I'll attach a 1-page topology diagram and the perf model in a follow-up note (linked). If Ellis is comfortable, we can kick off procurement discussions in parallel.

-Karthik
